text: An astounding show of support today for Lindsay Clancy. Hundreds of women, all dressed in pink, cheered the accused mom as she arrived in a police caravan for her murder trial. Supporters ran across the field to greet Lindsay. Some came with their babies. 19 days before Lindsay Clancy killed all three of her children, she was discharged from one of the top psychiatric hospitals in America. And literally the day before the killings, she spoke to her own psychiatrist. Neither diagnosed her with psychosis. So did multiple mental health professionals completely miss what was happening to Lindsay? Or was there simply no psychosis for them to see? Let's go back. Lindsay had struggled with anxiety before, and had even seen a therapist after her second child was born. But after Callan, her third kid, was born in May 2022, things actually seemed pretty good at first. Patrick had 12 weeks of paternity leave and described that summer as great. Lindsay was supposed to return to work only in the fall. But as that date approached, her anxiety got significantly worse. She extended her leave and eventually never returned to work. Then came severe insomnia, depression, and increasingly serious mental health problems. Over the next four months, Lindsay was prescribed 13 different psychiatric medications. You might have seen that number online, but it doesn't mean she was taking all 13 at once. Different drugs were started, stopped, and adjusted by multiple providers. By December, Patrick described Lindsay as being in a big spiral. She was severely sleep-deprived, increasingly depressed, and talking about suicide. And most importantly, she told Patrick, she was having intrusive thoughts about harming the children. Patrick asked whether she thought she needed to stay away from them. She said no. According to him, Lindsay could describe these horrible thoughts and then go back to caring for the children normally. He had never seen her hurt them. And despite claims online that Patrick simply failed her, the evidence shows he was trying to get her help. He helped her seek treatment, push for more intensive care, and when Lindsay was scared to go to McLean Hospital, Patrick testified that he told her, you have to go. So on January 1st, Lindsay voluntarily entered McLean. At the time, ranked number one in America for psychiatric care. Today, Lindsay's defense says she was suffering from psychosis. In simple terms, psychosis means losing touch with reality. For example, hearing voices or strongly believing things that aren't true. Someone who is psychotic can still sometimes appear relatively normal. But the psychiatrist who treated Lindsay at McLean did not diagnose psychosis. She diagnosed severe major depressive disorder without psychotic features. She testified that Lindsay showed no signs of psychosis and denied having a plan to kill herself or harm anyone else. She also said Lindsay never reported thoughts of harming anybody else during her stay. Lindsay was discharged from McLean on January 5th. But just one day later, her regular psychiatrist, Dr. Jennifer Tufts, noted that Lindsay appeared to be deteriorating. She was still depressed and feeling numb. Tufts continued seeing her throughout the months while adjusting her medication. But despite Lindsay clearly still struggling, Tufts said she never saw signs of psychosis or mania. And importantly, Tufts did not know Lindsay had told Patrick about thoughts of harming the children. And later said that information would have concerned her greatly. Then on January 23rd, the day before the killings, Tufts spoke with Lindsay again. Lindsay said she felt numb and had no motivation, but denied suicidal or homicidal thoughts. The next day, all three children were dead. Patrick also testified that nobody treating Lindsay had ever told him not to leave the children alone with her. So what exactly happened here? Did one of America's top psychiatric hospitals and Lindsay's own psychiatrist somehow miss her psychosis? Did Lindsay only become psychotic after leaving McLean? Was she already experiencing psychotic symptoms, but simply wasn't telling anyone? Or was she never psychotic at all? And the psychosis explanation came only after she killed her children. Because after the killings, Lindsay described something none of her doctors apparently knew about. She said she had been hearing a male voice. And what she says that voice told her is probably the most important piece of evidence in this case.
